acceptanceCriteria.statement: Framing a body STICKS. After asking for a body at a given multiple of its radius, the camera is still there many frames later — on the game's ORRERY and on the lab page. The claim is only accepted alongside a positive control proving the old direct-write path drifts over the same interval, because the failure this replaces reports success while the camera walks away.

verifyVia.input: In the game: `_lab.spawnProceduralSystem('lab-procedural-6')` then `_lab.frameBody({kind:'planet', p:3}, {radii:2})`. In the lab: `_lab.frameBody({radii:2})`. Wait >=30 rendered frames on each, then re-measure.
verifyVia.observable: Achieved distance-in-radii after >=30 frames is within 1% of the value the call returned, on BOTH front-ends. POSITIVE CONTROL, same page, same interval: the pre-existing path (game `_lab.setCameraPose`, lab direct `camera.position.set`) drifts well outside that band — proving the stability is a real null and not an unmoved instrument.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The call reports what it ACHIEVED, not what was asked. Both front-ends clamp the near end — the lab's `minCameraDistance(sVis)` only ever raises distance, and the game holds a radius*1.05 zoom floor — so at exactly the close radii Max cares about, asked and achieved diverge. The returned number is the achieved one, measured in the renderer's own frame.

verifyVia.input: Ask for a radius BELOW the near-end clamp on each front-end (e.g. `{radii: 1.0}`), and for one comfortably above it (`{radii: 8}`).
verifyVia.observable: For the below-clamp ask, the returned `achieved.radii` differs from the asked value and equals an independent measurement taken from the live scene graph via `getWorldPosition`/`getWorldScale` (the rebase-immune method `_lab.shotState().geometry.distanceRadii` already uses) to within 1%. For the above-clamp ask, asked and achieved agree to within 1%. No call ever echoes the asked value back as though it were achieved.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The call reports the LOD state it produced, with the renderer's LIVE uniform values and the values predicted from the achieved distance reported SEPARATELY — so a disagreement between them is visible rather than averaged away. This is what turns a side-by-side into two pictures with numbers attached.

verifyVia.input: `_lab.frameBody({kind:'planet', p:3}, {radii:2})` on a generated system, then the same against a PLANET-CLASS MOON.
verifyVia.observable: The return carries live `uOctaves`/`uLodRamp` read off the body's material AND `predicted.octaves`/`predicted.ramp` computed by `lodRampOf`/`autoOctaves` (imported from `planet-lod-lab-core.js`, the shared law) from the achieved radii — as separate fields. On the planet, they agree. On the planet-class moon they DISAGREE — live `uOctaves` reads its 4.0 default against a higher predicted value — surfacing the unregistered-moon defect at `src/main.js:7437` (`lodManager.register(moon)` sits in the `else` arm) instead of concealing it.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The whole approach comes back in one call. Walking a body from far out down to nearly touching it produces a table — one row per step, each with achieved radius and the LOD state at that radius — on both front-ends. This is the row of numbers that answers 'does detail keep resolving, or am I flying at a beach ball?'

verifyVia.input: `_lab.approachSweep({kind:'planet', p:3}, {from:20, to:1.2, steps:8})` in the game, and the lab-page equivalent.
verifyVia.observable: Returns 8 rows, each carrying achieved radii (monotonically decreasing) plus live and predicted LOD state. The table PRINTS the saturation: rows at and below 6 body radii all show predicted octaves pinned at 9.0 while achieved radii keep shrinking. Both front-ends produce a table of the same shape over the same ladder, so rows can be paired.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Stars and moons are reachable, not just planets — and widening body resolution to reach stars does not disturb any existing planet or moon resolution.

verifyVia.input: On a fixed seed: `_lab.frameBody({kind:'star', s:0}, {radii:4})`, `_lab.frameBody({kind:'moon', p:1, m:0}, {radii:3})`, plus `_lab.resolveBody({kind:'planet', p:0})` and `_lab.shotState()` run before and after the change.
verifyVia.observable: Star and moon framings succeed and report achieved radii against the correct body's own radius (stars carry radius on `data.radius`, not derived from geometry — the two paths must not be conflated). REGRESSION: `resolveBody` for every existing `{kind:'planet'|'moon'}` subject returns identical `name`/`kind`/`p`/`m`/`backLink`, and `shotState()`'s `body` and `geometry` blocks are unchanged field for field.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The interpolator resync cannot be silently removed. The defect this workstream exists to end is a missing `cameraInterp.resync(camera)` whose absence produces a confident success report, so its presence is held by a gate that fails when it is deleted.

verifyVia.input: Run the test suite; then run it again against a mutant with the `resync` call deleted from the game-side framing path.
verifyVia.observable: A headless source-scan gate (the repo's existing `source-scan.mjs` idiom) asserts the game framing path calls `cameraInterp.resync`. It PASSES on the real source and FAILS on the mutant — a moved control, not an assertion that merely holds.

inputs: src/camera/ShipCameraSystem.js:662 `focusOn(position, viewDistance)` — the supported framing path; snaps `distance` AND `smoothedDistance` so `_applyOrbit()` places the camera FROM that state instead of fighting it. Has no `window._lab` hook today, which is exactly why it was unreachable.
src/core/CameraInterpolator.js:91 `resync(camera)` — the module's documented announcement for a teleport discontinuity; collapses both snapshots so the next blend is a no-op.

src/main.js `_lab.resolveBody` — NAME-keyed body resolution over the SIM tree. The single resolution path, deliberately: two index spaces are live at once and resolving through the scene walk instead frames body X while driving body Y, with both hooks reporting success.

planet-lod-lab-core.js `lodRampOf` / `autoOctaves` — the shared LOD law, already imported by both `BodyRenderer.js:11` and `LabPlanetMaterial.js`. Predicted LOD state is computed from these, never re-derived.
planet-lod-lab.html state.distance / state.yaw / state.pitch — the lab's frame loop reads these every frame; `state.distance` is ALREADY expressed in planet radii (logical = state.distance / sVis).
outputs: `_lab.frameBody(subject, opts)` on BOTH front-ends — returns `{ok, achieved:{radii, units}, lod:{live:{octaves,ramp}, predicted:{octaves,ramp}}, body:{name,kind,p,m}}`.
`_lab.approachSweep(subject, {from, to, steps})` on both front-ends — the per-step measurement table.
Paired A/B stills framed by identical code on both front-ends, with the LOD state that produced them attached — the input PLAN §LAYER 7 (approach detail) needs before it can start.
Evidence of the unregistered-planet-class-moon defect, as a live/predicted disagreement rather than a claim.
mustStayWorking: `_lab.shotState()` — its `body`, `geometry` and `roi` blocks are the sidecar contract `scripts/shot-diff.mjs` refuses to run without. Widening `resolveBody` to stars must leave every existing field byte-identical for planet and moon subjects.

`_lab.setCameraPose` / `cameraPose` — the existing A/B pose-replay pair. Keep working; they are how prior shots are reproduced. (`setCameraPose` should gain the missing `resync`, which CHANGES its behaviour from broken to correct — that is a fix, and it must be called out rather than slipped in.)

ORRERY <-> HELM mode ownership. `focusOn` is an orbit-camera method; the M-swap already clears ORRERY focus state (`_gliding`, `resetFocusMinDistance()`) so a focus min-distance cannot leak into HELM's supercruise-exit clamp. A framing API that pins focus state must not defeat that clearing.
The arrival-zoom path — `focusOn` calls `_endArrival(false)` by design (a focus-snap cancels a live arrival zoom, AC4). Framing during a spawn's arrival zoom must not leave the zoom half-cancelled.
All four instruments green (`npm run check:instruments`), citations at 320. Any new file carrying symbol-anchored citations lands inside the fence's coverage.
The known-failure baseline of 24 failed / 17 failed FILES / 22685 passed is GREEN — do not read those as damage.
